# `js/jsdoc-check-tag-names`

**Known JSDoc tag names, written the preferred way**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/jsdoc` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `defined_tags`, `inline_tags`, `jsx_tags` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/check-tag-names` |

## What it checks

Every block tag is one the plugin's default (TypeScript) mode knows — JSDoc's, TSDoc's, TypeDoc's and TypeScript's own (`@import`, `@overload`, `@satisfies`, `@template`) — and an alias is written as its preferred tag: `@return` is `@returns`, `@arg` and `@argument` are `@param`, `@prop` is `@property`, `@extends` is `@augments`, `@const` is `@constant`, `@func` and `@method` are `@function`, `@desc` is `@description`, `@exception` is `@throws`, `@yield` is `@yields`, `@virtual` is `@abstract`. An inline tag (`{@link …}`) is one of `link`, `linkcode`, `linkplain`, `tutorial`, `inheritDoc`, `label`, `include`, `includeCode`. A tag inside a fenced code block is not read. The upstream `typed` option and its `tagNamePreference` setting are not read: the preferred names are the plugin's defaults, and `defined_tags` adds tags the project uses.

**Why:** A misspelt tag is silently dropped by documentation tools, and two spellings of one tag make a codebase's docs hard to search.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/jsdoc` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/jsdoc"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defined_tags` | `string[]` | `[]` | tags the project uses besides the built-in ones |
| `inline_tags` | `string[]` | `[]` | inline tags allowed besides the built-in ones |
| `jsx_tags` | `boolean` | `false` | allow @jsx, @jsxFrag, @jsxImportSource and @jsxRuntime |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names".options]
defined_tags = []
inline_tags = []
jsx_tags = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = { severity = "error", options = { defined_tags = ["note"], inline_tags = ["<name>"], jsx_tags = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `defined_tags`

*string[]* · default `[]`

tags the project uses besides the built-in ones

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names".options]
defined_tags = ["note"]
```

#### `inline_tags`

*string[]* · default `[]`

inline tags allowed besides the built-in ones

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names".options]
inline_tags = ["<name>"]
```

#### `jsx_tags`

*boolean* · default `false`

allow @jsx, @jsxFrag, @jsxImportSource and @jsxRuntime

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names".options]
jsx_tags = true
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-check-tag-names.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### defined_tags adds a tag

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-check-tag-names".options]
defined_tags = ["note"]
```

```js
/**
 * @note hi
 */
function f() {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = { options = { defined_tags = ["note"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-check-tag-names" = { severity = "warn", options = { defined_tags = ["note"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-check-tag-names": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"defined_tags": ["note"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-check-tag-names: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-check-tag-names expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-check-tag-names --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-check-tag-names       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-check-tag-names  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>            # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Write the alias as its preferred tag (`@returns`, `@param`, `@property`).
2. Fix a misspelt tag, or list a tag the project uses on purpose in the rule's `defined_tags` option.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
/**
 * Gets the name.
 * @return {string} the name
 */
function getName() {}
```

#### Do

```js
/**
 * Gets the name.
 * @returns {string} the name
 */
function getName() {}
```

#### Fixed

```js
/**
 * Gets the name.
 * @returns {string} the name
 */
function getName() {}
```
